title: Claude Is Kirk. Codex Is Spock. Run Them in Pairs.
keywords: AI pair programming with two agents
when AI agents lie to themselves
description: Two-agent pairing as a working pattern. Claude (Kirk) is the actor — fast at implementation, prone to confusion loops on hard analysis, sometimes believing its own invented "truths" that it secretly documents somewhere. Codex (Spock) is the skeptic — ultra-conservative, will not act without explicit instruction, naturally assumes the analytical role of figuring out whether claims are evidence-based. The dispatch argues for putting them in dialogue rather than picking one. Worked example: GitHub issue #315 in this repo — long Claude/Codex back-and-forth on a real problem; Codex breaks Claude out of a death spiral and demands evidence. Failure modes the dispatch will name: (1) operator picks one agent and rationalizes its weaknesses; (2) operator runs both but in parallel rather than dialogue, missing the audit. Pairs naturally with `socratic-coding-agents` — both are about agent behavior at the interaction layer.
